authoredFrom: ER-D34, from the FULL 4,326-file corpus draw (the 4,000-file stride sample had 0 missing, so this class was invisible until every file was run). otp/lib/kernel/test/file_SUITE.erl is the only file in the corpus that names itself through a macro, and it failed silently and totally: `-module(?FILE_SUITE).` parses as a module_attribute whose only named child is a macro_call_expr, and a reader that requires an `atom` emitted NO module symbol at all. The file then fell back to being owned by its PATH, so its ownership, its export matching and its cross-module identity were all wrong with no error anywhere. Common Test suites do this by convention. Lines read off this file.

expectSymbols.name: modname_macro_er3
expectSymbols.note: the module is named by what the macro EXPANDS TO, never by the macro's own name

expectRelationships.note: a macro use is a macro use wherever it appears — including in -module(...)
